hook.en: A few per cent difference in growth each year does not sound like much. Over a decade it can decide whether a country's output nearly doubles or nearly triples.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಷ ಕೆಲವು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಸಣ್ಣದೆನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹತ್ತು ವರ್ಷಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅದು ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟೋ ಮೂರುಪಟ್ಟೋ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Compare the GDP growth of India, China and Pakistan
Compare the sectoral sources of growth
Use compounding to compare growth paths

narration.en: A few per cent difference in growth each year does not sound like much. Over a decade it can decide whether a country's output nearly doubles or nearly triples.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಷ ಕೆಲವು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಸಣ್ಣದೆನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹತ್ತು ವರ್ಷಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅದು ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟೋ ಮೂರುಪಟ್ಟೋ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: China has had double-digit growth for a long period. In 1980–90, China's GDP grew at about 10.3 per cent a year, Pakistan's at about 6.3 per cent and India's at about 5.7 per cent; in the 1980s Pakistan was ahead of India. In the following decades China's growth stayed high but has since slowed, India's growth rose, and Pakistan's growth declined, partly because of political instability. Because growth compounds, even a few percentage points of difference widen into large gaps in income over time.

points.en: Pakistan ahead of India in the 1980s
Small growth gaps compound into large income gaps

narration.en: In the 1980s China grew at about 10.3 per cent a year, Pakistan at 6.3 and India at 5.7. Later India sped up while Pakistan slowed. Compounding turns small gaps into big ones.
narration.kn: 1980ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಚೀನಾ ಸುಮಾರು 10.3%, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ 6.3%, ಭಾರತ 5.7% ಬೆಳೆದವು. ನಂತರ ಭಾರತ ವೇಗ ಪಡೆಯಿತು, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ ನಿಧಾನವಾಯಿತು.

title.en: On the board: Growth of GDP, 1980–90

narration.en: Let us compare growth rates with bars, then see what compounding does.

say.en: Here are NCERT's annual GDP growth rates for 1980 to 1990.
India grew at about 5.7 per cent a year.
China grew at about 10.3 per cent, almost double.
Pakistan grew at about 6.3 per cent, a little ahead of India in the 1980s.
Compounding turns this gap into a giant one: starting at 100, after ten years China reaches about 267 and India about 174.

body.en: In all three countries the share of agriculture in GDP has fallen, though a large share of the workforce in India and Pakistan still depends on agriculture. China's growth has been driven mainly by the manufacturing and service sectors, and a big part of its workforce has moved out of farming into industry. India's growth has come mainly from the service sector, which has grown without a matching shift of workers out of agriculture. In Pakistan too the service sector has grown, while agricultural performance has been volatile.

narration.en: China grew mainly through manufacturing and services, India mainly through services, and Pakistan through services with an unstable farm sector. In India and Pakistan many workers still depend on agriculture.
narration.kn: ಚೀನಾ ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ, ಭಾರತ ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು. ಭಾರತ ಮತ್ತು ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಇನ್ನೂ ಅನೇಕರು ಕೃಷಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

caption.en: GDP index of two countries starting at 100, growing at a per cent and b per cent a year (NCERT 1980–90 rates: China 10.3, India 5.7, Pakistan 6.3).

narration.en: Set two growth rates and watch how quickly a gap of a few per cent becomes a huge gap in income.

tryThis.en: China 10.3 vs India 5.7: what are the two indexes after 10 years?
Set Pakistan 6.3 against India 5.7. Is the gap large after 20 years?
Check the rule of 70: at 7%, does the index double in about 10 years?

problem.en: Using NCERT's 1980–90 growth rates (China 10.3%, Pakistan 6.3%, India 5.7%), find each country's GDP index in 1990 if all three start at 100 in 1980.

steps.en: China's output grew about 2.7 times, India's about 1.7 times in the same decade.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Using NCERT's 1980–90 growth rates (China 10.3%, Pakistan 6.3%, India 5.7%), find each country's GDP index in 1990 if all three start at 100 in 1980.

body.en: To find roughly how many years an economy takes to double its GDP, divide 70 by its growth rate. China at 10.3% doubles in about 7 years; India at 5.7% in about 12 years.

narration.en: Rule of seventy: divide seventy by the growth rate to get the doubling time.

narration.kn: ತರಗತಿ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಕೈ ಎತ್ತಿ, ಮಾನಿಟರ್ ತರಗತಿಯ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಲಿ.

points.en: In 1980–90 China grew about 10.3% a year, Pakistan 6.3% and India 5.7%.
China's growth came from manufacturing and services; India's mainly from services.
points.kn: ಚೀನಾದ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ; ಭಾರತದ್ದು ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ.

points.en: Compounding turns small differences in growth into large differences in income.
points.kn: ಚಕ್ರಬಡ್ಡಿಯಂತೆ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ಸಣ್ಣ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಆದಾಯದಲ್ಲಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

homework.en: Compare the sectoral sources of growth in India, China and Pakistan.

narration.en: Recap. In 1980–90 China grew about 10.3% a year, Pakistan 6.3% and India 5.7%. China's growth came from manufacturing and services; India's mainly from services. Compounding turns small differences in growth into large differences in income.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. 1980-90ರಲ್ಲಿ ಚೀನಾ ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು 10.3%, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ 6.3%, ಭಾರತ 5.7% ಬೆಳೆದವು. ಚೀನಾದ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ; ಭಾರತದ್ದು ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಸೇವೆಗಳಿಂದ. ಚಕ್ರಬಡ್ಡಿಯಂತೆ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ಸಣ್ಣ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಆದಾಯದಲ್ಲಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.
